collection_summary: This instance is a curated, source-defined ground truth listing the top 20 largest lakes in the world by surface area, taken from the Wikipedia 'List of lakes by area' master article's Table[2] area-descending ranking. For each lake the staged row records the Continent (closed 6-value vocabulary), Type (closed 2-value Fresh/Saline), Area (km²) as integer, and Max. depth (m) as integer. The 20-row universe is the top-20 by Rank in the source's natural area-descending order — a hard rank-based filter with no curator-judgment on which lakes qualify. All 5 staged cells are derivable from the master Table[2] with only mechanical normalization (Area/Depth integer extraction from compound 'metric (imperial)' source format; Type closed-vocab normalization by stripping salinity-percentage suffixes; Continent derivation from Countries-with-shoreline using the dominant-continent rule). The schema is designed for top_k benchmark evaluation: Lake is the PK lookup target; all 4 attribute cells are exact-match-evaluable (Continent + Type from closed vocabularies, Area + Max. depth as numeric integers).
source_coverage_notes:
Roles:
- source_urls[0] (List_of_lakes_by_area): universe + filter + value (defines the master Table[2] area-descending wikitable; supplies the per-row Lake name verbatim from the Name column, base material for Continent via the Countries-with-shoreline column, base material for Type via the Type column with salinity-percentage normalization, Area (km²) as integer from the Area column's compound metric-imperial format, and Max. depth (m) as integer from the Max. depth column's compound metric-imperial format).

Single-source Tier B instance. The Wikipedia master article is the canonical authoritative compilation of lakes ranked by surface area. Per-row cells: Lake name is verbatim from the master Name column for all 20 rows. Continent is curator-derived from the Countries-with-shoreline cell using a closed 6-value vocabulary and the dominant-continent rule; the only non-trivial cases are the Caspian Sea (5 shoreline countries including transcontinental Russia, staged as Asia per 4-of-5 Asian-shoreline dominance) and Lake Vostok (subglacial under Antarctic ice, staged as Antarctica per geographic location). Type is curator-normalized from the master Type column to a closed 2-value vocabulary by stripping salinity-percentage suffixes ('Saline 1.2%' → 'Saline'; 'Saline 0.3% (variable)' → 'Saline'). Area (km²) and Max. depth (m) are integer values extracted from the master's compound 'metric (imperial)' source format with commas stripped. Cell-level audit can spot-check any of the 20 rows against the master Table[2]; no per-lake article fetches are needed because all 5 staged cells are derivable from the master table.
decision_log:
Candidate card (per instance_selection_priorities.md):
- Pre-gate verdict: Pass. Universe (top-20 largest lakes by surface area per Wikipedia 'List of lakes by area' Table[2]) is fully source-defined via the master article's natural rank ordering; per-row attribute cells are verbatim/lightly-normalized from the master table's columns. Table is LLM-knowable for a pre-2025 cutoff: very-LLM-knowable cells include the canonical great lakes (Caspian Sea, Superior, Victoria, Tanganyika, Baikal, Titicaca, Erie, Ontario); mid-difficulty cells include the well-known but less-headline-grabbing lakes (Huron, Michigan, Great Bear Lake, Great Slave Lake, Malawi, Ladoga, Winnipeg); harder calibration cells include the smaller named lakes (Balkhash, Vostok subglacial, Onega, Nicaragua, Athabasca). Row count (20) clears the 10-row gate.
- Seed/provenance: original instance, NOT from a seed in example_questions.txt. User selected lakes-by-area after a deep-dive on the multi_hop capitals-rivers alternative; capitals-rivers would have required curator-bounded universe + multi-source extraction (~30 per-capital articles), whereas lakes-by-area is single-source single-master-table with all cells exact-match-evaluable.
- Category: top_k (gap 2 before this staging — `top_k` at 3 of 5 with largest_islands_by_area_top20_britannica, top_10_most_populous_cities_per_continent, notable_bridges_by_main_span; this instance brings top_k to 4 of 5 — gap 2 → 1) primary; geographic (gap 3) secondary because the Continent column provides a geographic axis. Per references/artifact-contract.md, top_k pairs canonically with operation_type=top_k (when the schema is a rank-truncated SELECT over an ordered universe); the db_analog 'SELECT lake, continent, type, area_km2, max_depth_m FROM lakes ORDER BY area_km2 DESC LIMIT 20' is the canonical top-K-by-numeric-attribute primitive.
- Source plan: Tier B Wikipedia, single source URL; gt_construction = manual_wikipedia; source_count = 1 (master 'List of lakes by area' article supplies all 5 cells per row via its Table[2]).
- Expected shape: 20 rows × 5 columns; PK = Lake.
- Domain: Geography/Lakes — NEW Lakes subdomain extending the Geography family from 11 to 12 instances. Existing Geography subdomains: Cities, Countries, Islands, Deserts, Mountaineering, Hydrology (×2 transboundary-rivers), Climate, Linguistics, Politics, Oceans. NEW Lakes joins Hydrology + Oceans + Deserts as the third physical-water-or-landform subdomain.
- Entity class: physical-features/lakes — NEW fine-class extending the physical-features bucket from 6 fine-classes (mountains, rivers, deserts, islands, oceanic-trenches, +1 historical) to 7. Entity-class novelty axis score: strong (NEW fine-class within a bucket that already has multi-fine-class representation but no lakes entry).
- Risks/adaptation: (a) Caspian Sea classification — the source's Notes column explicitly addresses the lake-vs-ocean question and rules in favor of including the Caspian as a lake per surface-area-ranking convention; staged accordingly. (b) Caspian Continent normalization — 5 shoreline countries span the Asia-Europe boundary (Iran, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Azerbaijan, Russia); staged as 'Asia' per dominant 4-of-5 Asian-shoreline rule. (c) Vostok subglacial lake — staged with Continent = 'Antarctica' per geographic location despite being beneath the ice sheet rather than at surface. (d) Type normalization drops salinity-percentage suffixes; the closed 2-value Fresh/Saline vocabulary loses fine-grained salinity information present in source (Saline 0.3% vs 1.2% etc.). (e) Area and Max. depth values are bathymetric-survey-dependent and may be revised in future Wikipedia updates; staged values match source as of accession date.
- Decision: Stage.

Why original rather than seed-driven: no seed in example_questions.txt targets lakes or physical-feature top-K ranking instances.

Why 'top-20 by area' universe rather than alternatives: deep-dive on universe design considered 3 options. Option A (top-10 by area) would only have 10 rows at the row-count-gate floor and would miss the bottom-half geographic diversity (no European Onega, no South American Titicaca beyond rank-18). Option B (top-15 by area) would also miss Titicaca (rank 18) and Vostok (rank 16). Option C (top-20 by area, the chosen design) clears the row-count gate comfortably, captures the well-known European Onega + South American Titicaca + Antarctic Vostok bottom-half lakes, and produces a clean 6-continent distribution (10/3/3/2/1/1). Option D (top-25 by area) was rejected because the rank-21-to-25 lakes are smaller and less LLM-knowable (Reindeer, Turkana, Issyk-Kul, Vänern, Rukwa).

Category ↔ operation_type pairing: top_k pairs canonically with operation_type=top_k per references/artifact-contract.md. The 5-attribute SELECT per row over a rank-truncated universe is the canonical top-K primitive (matching largest_islands_by_area_top20_britannica's same 'top-20-by-area' pattern with a different physical-feature entity class).

Domain selection: Geography/Lakes — NEW Lakes subdomain. Geography is already the largest domain (11 instances tied with Science), but Lakes is a NEW subdomain that complements the existing physical-water-or-landform subdomains (Hydrology, Oceans, Deserts). Per domain_taxonomy.md, the Lakes subdomain is appropriate for lake-keyed physical-feature instances.

Entity class selection: physical-features/lakes — NEW fine-class within the physical-features bucket. The bucket was at 6 fine-classes before this staging (mountains, rivers ×2 instances, deserts, islands, oceanic-trenches); this instance brings it to 7 with NEW lakes. NEW fine-class scores strong on the Entity-class novelty axis per the 4-axis selection rubric.

Claim type: source_defined — the universe is fully defined by the master article's natural rank-based ordering (top-20 by Area). The curator does NOT supplement the universe with non-Table[2] lakes. All 5 staged cells are derivable from the master article with only mechanical normalization (Area/Depth integer extraction, Type closed-vocab normalization, Continent derivation from Countries-shoreline cell).

Post-audit (2026-05-14, cycle 1): cycle-1 audit verdict 'Ready' — 0 BLOCKING, 1 NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE, 0 SUGGESTION. The data itself is source-faithful (20-row top-K universe matches the cited ranking from Caspian Sea rank-1 through Athabasca rank-20; Reindeer correctly excluded at rank-21; PK unique; Area-sort desc intact; closed vocabs intact with all 6 continents populated; Type 18/2 distribution correct). The single residual hygiene item was prose-only Type normalization text: (a) curation.json::normalization_decisions Type-normalization sentence had a stale 'Fresh (15 rows: ...)' count followed by '— 18 rows' parenthetical, listing 18 lake names but mismatching the leading count claim; (b) draft.json::temporal_note Type-normalization-examples sentence included 'Saline 0.25% (approx.)' (rank-22 Turkana) and 'Saline 0.6%' (rank-23 Issyk-Kul) as example values when those lakes are outside the staged top-20 universe. Resolved by: (i) rewriting normalization_decisions Type-normalization sentence to lead with the actual staged Saline pair (Caspian + Balkhash, 2 rows) and explicit 'the other 18 rows are Fresh verbatim' clarification, with the rank-22/23/25 Saline forms mentioned only as out-of-universe context; (ii) rewriting temporal_note Type-normalization examples to list only the staged-universe Saline cells (Caspian Sea 'Saline 1.2%' and Balkhash 'Saline 0.3% (variable)') and drop the out-of-universe Turkana/Issyk-Kul examples. Net cycle-1 changes: 2 prose-section scrubs on Type-normalization examples; no CSV / source_count / row count / schema / distribution changes (still 20 rows × 5 cols, source_count 1, Lake PK unique, Area-desc sort intact, Type Fresh 18 / Saline 2 distribution intact).

Post-audit (2026-05-14, cycle 2): cycle-2 verification audit verdict 'Ready+Clean' — 0 BLOCKING, 0 NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE, 0 SUGGESTION. The cycle-1 Type-normalization prose fix confirmed clean: both normalization_decisions and temporal_note now consistently describe the in-universe 2-Saline (Caspian + Balkhash) + 18-Fresh split, with rank-22/23/25 Saline forms clearly framed as out-of-universe context. Data state confirmed: 20-row CSV unchanged, schema columns unchanged, Lake PK unique, Area-descending sort intact, closed Continent + Type vocabularies intact with the same distributions, source_count = 1. Instance marked accept-ready as of 2026-05-14. Total cycle count: 3 (cycle-0 staging + cycles 1-2 audit/repair). Universe stable at 20 events across all cycles; the single repair was a prose-only narrative-alignment scrub (no CSV/schema/source-set changes). The instance chips `top_k` from gap 2 to **gap 1** (4 of 5 staged) and adds Geography/Lakes as a NEW subdomain, extending the Geography family from 11 to 12 instances. NEW `physical-features/lakes` fine-class extends the physical-features bucket from 6 to 7 fine-classes. Useful reference: top_k-by-numeric-attribute instances with sub-universe scope (top-N cutoff on a longer master list) require explicit in-universe-vs-out-of-universe framing in normalization_decisions when discussing closed-vocab values that appear in source rows beyond the rank cutoff; the cycle-1 hygiene pattern here (Saline examples from ranks 22/23/25 wrongly presented as in-universe values) is a generalizable pitfall to flag at Stage-1 for future top_k instances.

Metadata fix (2026-06-02, structural): operation_type top_k→projection; top_k is NOT in the OPERATION_TYPES enum (curation_ui/app.py:60 lists exactly {join, union, intersect, projection, union+filter, filter, aggregation}). The prior cycle-1/cycle-2 audits and the earlier 'Category ↔ operation_type pairing' note in this decision_log asserted that 'top_k pairs canonically with operation_type=top_k per references/artifact-contract.md' — that assertion is incorrect: the artifact-contract has no top_k operation_type, and an invalid value silently coerces to index-0 'join' if the instance is opened in the curation UI (app.py:1388-1391) and is flagged by validate_operation_query_pair (app.py:655-675). projection is the contract-valid pairing for query_category=top_k because db_analog is a pure ranked column-selection (SELECT lake, continent, type, area_km2, max_depth_m FROM lakes ORDER BY area_km2 DESC LIMIT 20 — ORDER BY <attr> DESC LIMIT K with NO WHERE predicate), so the structural primitive is a multi-column SELECT (projection), not a filter. Verified projection ∈ validate_operation_query_pair allowed set for top_k = {projection, filter, union+filter}. No CSV rows, query_category (still top_k), secondary_category, primary_key, column_types, db_analog logic, source_count, or source_urls changed; only operation_type + this decision_log entry.
normalization_decisions: Universe definition: the staged universe is the 20 lakes occupying ranks 1-20 in the Wikipedia 'List of lakes by area' master article's Table[2] area-descending wikitable (tables[2] per pandas.read_html, 47-row master ordered by Area km² descending). The rank cutoff is mechanical (the source's own rank-1 to rank-20 selection). The 20 staged lakes are: Caspian Sea (rank 1), Superior (2), Victoria (3), Huron (4), Michigan (5), Tanganyika (6), Baikal (7), Great Bear Lake (8), Malawi/Nyasa (9), Great Slave Lake (10), Erie (11), Winnipeg (12), Ontario (13), Ladoga (14), Balkhash (15), Vostok (16), Onega (17), Titicaca (18), Nicaragua (19), Athabasca (20). Lake name normalization: each row's Lake is taken verbatim from the master Name column. 'Caspian Sea' is staged verbatim per source (Notes column rules in favor of including the Caspian Sea as a lake despite its 'small ocean' classification, on surface-area-ranking convention grounds); 'Great Bear Lake' and 'Great Slave Lake' include the 'Lake' suffix per source convention; 'Malawi (Nyasa)' preserves source's parenthetical alternate name; 'Vostok' is staged as the bare name per source despite being a subglacial lake (Lake Vostok is the canonical name but source uses 'Vostok'). Continent normalization: each row's Continent is curator-derived from the master's 'Countries with shoreline' column using a closed 6-value vocabulary (Africa / Antarctica / Asia / Europe / North America / South America) with these rules: (i) lakes with all shoreline-countries on a single continent take that continent (Superior/Huron/Michigan/Erie/Ontario: 2 countries both North American → North America); (ii) lakes with shoreline countries spanning multiple continents take the dominant-continent (Caspian Sea: 5 shoreline countries including Iran/Kazakhstan/Turkmenistan/Azerbaijan all wholly or primarily Asian, plus Russia which is transcontinental with Caspian shoreline in its southern transcontinental region — staged as Asia per 4-of-5 dominant-Asian rule); (iii) subglacial Lake Vostok is staged with Continent = Antarctica per geographic location under the Antarctic ice sheet. Type normalization: each row's Type is curator-normalized from the master's Type column to a closed 2-value vocabulary (Fresh / Saline) by stripping salinity-percentage suffixes and clarifying-phrase additions. Within the staged top-20 universe, only 2 rows are Saline (rank-1 Caspian Sea 'Saline 1.2%' → 'Saline'; rank-15 Balkhash 'Saline 0.3% (variable)' → 'Saline'); the other 18 rows are 'Fresh' verbatim (Superior, Victoria, Huron, Michigan, Tanganyika, Baikal, Great Bear Lake, Malawi, Great Slave Lake, Erie, Winnipeg, Ontario, Ladoga, Vostok, Onega, Titicaca, Nicaragua, Athabasca — 18 rows). The closed 2-value vocab loses fine-grained salinity information present in source (other Saline forms appear at ranks 22 Turkana 'Saline 0.25% (approx.)', 23 Issyk-Kul 'Saline 0.6%', and 25 Rukwa 'Saline' but those rows are outside the staged top-20 universe). Area (km²) normalization: each row's Area is the integer square-kilometre value extracted from the master Area column's compound '###,### km2 ###,### sq mi' formulation — the km² metric prefix component is taken, comma-stripped, and converted to integer. Examples: '389,000 km2 150,000 sq mi' → 389000; '82,100 km2 31,700 sq mi[14]' → 82100; '7,850 km2 3,030 sq mi' → 7850. The square-mile imperial-suffix component is dropped; the [14] reference footnote (a Britannica reference used for Great Lakes Type/Area/Depth/Volume cells in the source) is also stripped. Max. depth (m) normalization: each row's Max. depth is the integer metre value extracted from the master Max. depth column's compound '###,### m ###,### ft' formulation — the m metric prefix component is taken, comma-stripped, and converted to integer. Examples: '1,025 m 3,363 ft' → 1025; '406 m 1,332 ft[14]' → 406; '1,642 m 5,387 ft' → 1642; '26 m 85 ft' → 26. The foot imperial-suffix component is dropped; the [14] reference footnote is stripped. All 20 staged depth values are integers. Sort order: the CSV is sorted **by Area (km²) descending** (= the source's natural Rank ascending = rank-1 Caspian Sea at row 1, rank-20 Athabasca at row 20). This sort matches the master article's natural area-ranking order. An alternative alphabetical-by-Lake sort was considered but rejected because area-ranking is the primary narrative dimension of this top_k-category instance (the 'top 20' framing is intrinsically rank-based).
open_questions: 1. Whether the Caspian Sea row should be retained as a lake (current staging, per source's Notes column ruling) or dropped per the 'small ocean' geological classification. The source explicitly addresses this question and includes the Caspian as rank-1 lake. 2. Whether the Caspian Sea Continent should be 'Asia' (current staging, per 4-of-5 Asian-shoreline dominance) or 'Asia/Europe' (open vocabulary allowing transcontinental labels) or 'Europe' (per the source's transcontinental Russia shoreline). 3. Whether Vostok subglacial lake should be staged with Continent = 'Antarctica' (current staging) or excluded per a 'surface lakes only' filter (would reduce universe to 19 rows). 4. Whether the Type column closed 2-value vocab (Fresh / Saline) is appropriate or whether the source's salinity-percentage information should be preserved (would open the closed vocabulary; alternative 4-value taxonomy could be Fresh / Brackish / Saline / Hypersaline). 5. Whether Area (km²) values should be stored as integers (current) or as floats with sub-km² precision (some source values have decimal precision like '5,614.7 km²' for Lake Rukwa rank-25, though no top-20 lakes have decimal Area values). 6. Whether the 'Great Bear Lake' and 'Great Slave Lake' rows should have the 'Lake' suffix in the Lake PK cell (current staging, per source) or be normalized to bare 'Great Bear' / 'Great Slave' (would match the source's other naming convention where Superior/Huron/Michigan are bare names). 7. Whether the universe should expand to top-25 by area (would add Reindeer, Turkana, Issyk-Kul, Vänern, Rukwa) or shrink to top-15 by area (would drop Vostok, Onega, Titicaca, Nicaragua, Athabasca). 8. Whether Lake Vostok's Type should be 'Fresh' (source claim, current staging) or flagged with subglacial qualifier — Vostok is fresh subglacial water but its accessibility/sampling is different from surface freshwater lakes.
